body: NFRD ANCHOR FEASIBILITY — SECOND BLOCKER, no shared edit and no lineage selection. I exported latest observed NFRD commit 99602baa only as a scratch probe at /tmp/storymodel4s-nfrd-anchor-probe.niVwMs. In the single assigned test path, sibling braced packages make a test-only internal anchor source-legal: classOf[NfrdBaseballSpec], classOf[VerifiedParticipant], classOf[NfrdBaseballReceipt], plus a singleton-typed value NfrdBaseballCourt.type. Baseline compiled and NfrdIntakePublicSuite passed 4/4. However, mutating only files.scala from private[bench] object NfrdBaseballCourt to public object, then rerunning incrementally with no clean, compiled exactly one main source and zero test sources; the external typeCheckErrors suite stayed stale and passed 4/4. A consumer-side wildcard import also remained stale under the same visibility-only mutation and adds an unused warning. This is not an adequate dependency anchor: the legal internal dependency remains lawful before and after the access widening, so Zinc does not invalidate the external compile-time macro court. The three class anchors may still be feasible for shape mutations, but the Court privacy refusal is not protected by this test-only anchor technique. Under the standing term “if an anchor cannot be added without touching production, stop and report,” I remain stopped. Chief decision now needs both a governing NFRD base and an explicit disposition for the privacy-only court: exclude it with the limitation recorded, authorize a different runtime/external-compiler court, or widen scope deliberately. No production/build/shared files touched.
